Level sensor breaks with growth-aware shifting

Source: R/breaks.R
dm_level_breaks.Rd

Applies user-defined break windows (sensor relocations, reinstallations, jumps) to a series: the in-break span is deleted and all post-break values are shifted so the level reconnects to the pre-break reference, plus a growth extrapolation estimated from the pre-break slope. The reference on each side of the break is the nearest non-NA value within growth_window_days (so a break endpoint sitting on a data gap does not poison the shift). One of the composable steps behind dm_clean_series().

Usage

dm_level_breaks(
  df,
  brks,
  grow_start_dm = "01-05",
  grow_end_dm = "31-10",
  growth_window_days = 14,
  growth_method = c("daily_lm", "10min_lm", "daily_robust", "10min_lm_flip"),
  allow_negative_growth = FALSE,
  max_slope_day = Inf,
  max_growth_total = Inf,
  tz = "UTC"
)

Arguments

df

Data.frame with columns series, ts, value.

brks

Named list: series name to a list of c(start, end) timestamp pairs. A flat unnamed list of pairs is accepted for a single-series df.

grow_start_dm, grow_end_dm

Growing-season start and end as "DD-MM" strings.

growth_window_days

Window (days) used for the slope estimate and the level-shift reference search around each break.

growth_method

Slope estimation method: one of "daily_lm", "10min_lm", "daily_robust", "10min_lm_flip".

allow_negative_growth

If FALSE, negative slope estimates are clamped to zero.

max_slope_day

Cap on the slope estimate (micrometres per day).

max_growth_total

Cap on the growth extrapolation per gap (micrometres).

tz

Timezone for timestamp coercion.

Value

df with breaks levelled (plus an internal .row_id ordering column added by the input validation).
